title: Mesquite Smoked Chuck Roast
seoTitle: Mesquite Smoked Chuck Roast | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Low-and-slow chuck roast sliced for sandwiches and plates for ten
subtitle: Low-and-slow chuck roast sliced for sandwiches and plates for ten
description: Beef chuck roasts get a simple salt-and-pepper crust, then smoke until probe-tender and sliceable. Rest, slice against the grain, and serve with quick pickles and soft rolls for a true smoke-night spread.

steps.title: Season the roasts
steps.instruction: Coat chuck roasts with mustard, then pack evenly with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika. Rest on a wire rack 30 minutes while the smoker preheats.

steps.title: Smoke until tender
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 250°F with mesquite or oak. Place roasts fat-side up and smoke until internal temperature reaches 165°F and a probe slides in with light resistance, about 5–6 hours. Target oven/smoker temperature: 250°F.

steps.title: Wrap and finish
steps.instruction: Wrap roasts in butcher paper and return to smoker until probe-tender at 203°F internal, about 1–1.5 hours more. Fat should render and meat should pull apart with gentle pressure. Target oven/smoker temperature: 250°F.

steps.title: Rest before slicing
steps.instruction: Rest wrapped roasts 30 minutes in a dry cooler or warm oven so juices redistribute. Unwrap and slice against the grain into quarter-inch portions.

steps.title: Hold and serve
steps.instruction: Toss sliced beef lightly with warm broth and vinegar. Hold covered at 165°F. Pile on rolls with pickles and extra pepper at the line.

proTips: Two smaller roasts cook more evenly than one massive roast and give you backup if one finishes early.
Save pan drippings, skim fat, and whisk into warmed broth for a quick au jus.
If bark gets too dark before tenderness, drop smoker temp to 225°F and stay patient.
tonightSpread: Sliced chuck on a hotel pan with soft rolls, dill pickles, and sliced raw onion.
Quick coleslaw with vinegar dressing to cut the rich smoke and fat.
leftovers: Chop and simmer in BBQ sauce for fast smoked beef sandwiches the next shift.
Dice into a hearty beef and barley soup with leftover broth.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Chuck roast delivers rich beef smoke flavor on a station budget. It shreds or slices cleanly, holds warm in hotel pans, and feeds a full hall without babysitting a brisket all day.
mealPrepNotes: Season roasts the night before uncovered on a rack so the rub sets. Bring to room temperature 45 minutes before smoking. Hold sliced beef at 165°F max with a splash of beef broth.
